title: Conormal fibre sequence for a smooth closed subscheme
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of $k$-schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-scheme-over-base], with $Z$ smooth over $k$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Write $\Omega_{X/k}$ and $\Omega_{Z/k}$ for the relative differential sheaves [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf]. For $z\in Z$, set $x=i(z)$, $R=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, $S=\mathcal O_{Z,z}$, $I=\ker(R\twoheadrightarrow S)$ and $\kappa=\kappa(z)$ [def-weil-residue-field]. Then the canonical sequence of $\kappa$-vector spaces
$$0\longrightarrow (I/I^2)\otimes_S\kappa\longrightarrow \Omega_{X/k,x}\otimes_R\kappa\longrightarrow \Omega_{Z/k,z}\otimes_S\kappa\longrightarrow0$$
is exact. The first arrow sends $(f\bmod I^2)\otimes1$ to $df\otimes1$ for every $f\in I$; the second is induced by the local-ring map $R\to S$. Here $I/I^2$ is the quotient of $I$ by the submodule generated by products of two elements of $I$, and the tensors are module base changes [def-weil-module-base-change].

source.place: Tag 06AA (lemma-differentials-relative-immersion-smooth): short exact conormal sequence for an immersion with source smooth over the base; passage to the residue field preserves exactness because the smooth differential sheaf on Z is locally free (Tag 02G1, lemma-smooth-omega-finite-locally-free).

proof.text: Work with the actual stalk rings R = O_X,i(z), S = O_Z,z and K = kappa(z). Give R and S their k-algebra structures via global constants and the germ map. IsOver and the germ/stalk-map identity give the scalar tower k -> R -> S. A closed immersion gives a surjection R -> S. Smoothness gives formal smoothness of the stalk map from O_Spec(k),f(z); the latter stalk is canonically k, so S is formally smooth over k. No finite-presentation claim about the stalk algebra is needed.

source.place: Tag 06AA, conormal exact sequence for an immersion smooth over the base; implemented directly on stalks using formal smoothness and the universal property of relative differentials.

proof.text: Identify the stalk of relative differentials over k with the Kahler differentials of the stalk ring. Taking stalks of the universal sheaf derivation gives a k-derivation of R. Conversely, every k-derivation R -> N defines a sheaf derivation into the skyscraper module at the point: on each neighborhood apply the derivation to the germ. The stalk-skyscraper adjunction and the universal property of relative differentials yield the inverse linear map. The two universal properties show that the composites are identities. The identification sends every differential germ da to D(germ(a)). Extend these linear equivalences to K.

source.place: Tag 06AA, conormal exact sequence for an immersion smooth over the base; implemented directly on stalks using formal smoothness and the universal property of relative differentials.

proof.text: Apply the algebraic conormal right exact sequence to k -> R -> S. Lift id_S along the square-zero surjection R/I^2 -> S by formal smoothness of S. The Mathlib equivalence retractionKerCotangentToTensorEquivSection turns this section into a retraction of I/I^2 -> S tensor_R Omega_R/k. This is the derivation construction from Algebra Tag 02HP and does not require smoothness of R. Regard the retraction as S-linear by surjectivity of R -> S.

source.place: Tag 06AA, conormal exact sequence for an immersion smooth over the base; implemented directly on stalks using formal smoothness and the universal property of relative differentials.

proof.text: Tensor the conormal maps and their retraction with K over S. The retraction identity survives base change, proving injectivity of the first map; right exactness of tensor products gives middle exactness and surjectivity of the last map. Surjectivity of R -> S gives compatible scalar multiplication on I/I^2, identifying K tensor_R I/I^2 with K tensor_S I/I^2. Cancel iterated base change in the middle term. The algebraic generator formulas give alpha(1 tensor [a]) = 1 tensor Da and beta(1 tensor Da) = 1 tensor D(a mod I).

source.place: Tag 06AA, conormal exact sequence for an immersion smooth over the base; implemented directly on stalks using formal smoothness and the universal property of relative differentials.

proof.text: Transport the two algebraic maps through the differential-stalk fibre equivalences. Linear equivalences preserve injectivity, exactness and surjectivity. Their germ formulas identify the first arrow on kernel elements. The identity germ_X(a) mapped by i.stalkMap = germ_Z(i.app(a)) proves exactly the stated formula for the second arrow. These are the actual stalk kernel, residue field, relative differential sheaves and section germs in the unchanged statement.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q109-cc85a3a40 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and all 8 steps in full, along with every cited statement. The delivery has no new nodes. The statement agrees with Stacks morphisms.tex:7429 (Tag 06AA), specialized to a closed immersion over k and taken at the fibre at z. X is arbitrary, Z is smooth and z need not be closed; both arrows are stated. I tested it on four cases: Spec k inside the dual numbers (characteristic 2 too), the origin of the cuspidal cubic y^2=x^3, the generic point of a line in A^2, and J=0. Step 1 uses parts (1) and (2) of the closed-immersion criterion leaf. Step 2 lifts through the formal-smoothness clause of def-sbc-smooth-morphisms on the affine first-order thickening Spec B in Spec A/J^2. The lift factors through V because K is nilpotent, and pi sigma = id. Step 3 is the Jacobi-Zariski leaf with (k,A,J); only the right exactness is taken from it. Step 4 is the 02HP derivation D(a)=(a mod J^2)-sigma(a-bar) (algebra.tex:34158); I checked the product calculation and tau delta = id. Steps 5-6 give the splitting identities, which survive tensoring with kappa by functoriality, so no flatness is needed. Step 7 is correct: affine-open stalk (c), the Spec-map stalk lemma and quotient localization give I=JR, and I checked the inverse of the conormal localization map. Step 8 is correct: tilde stalks identify the differentials, and d(j/t)=t^-1 dj - j t^-2 dt gives the first-arrow formula. proof_deps equals the union of the uses, and there is no cycle. Every theorem cited is a Mathlib leaf and the rest are definitions, so the sk-prop-an route is kept and no tool_uses are needed. lean.statement: theorem conormalStalkFibre_shortExact_of_smooth {k : Type u} [Field k] {X Z : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (.of k))] [Z.Over (Spec (.of k))] (i : Z ⟶ X) [i.IsOver (Spec (.of k))] [IsClosedImmersion i] [Smooth (Z ↘ Spec (.of k))] (z : Z) : ∃ (α : conormalStalkFibre i z →ₗ[Z.residueField z] relativeDifferentialsStalkFibre (X ↘ Spec (.of k)) i z) (β : relativeDifferentialsStalkFibre (X ↘ Spec (.of k)) i z →ₗ[Z.residueField z] relativeDifferentialsStalkFibre (Z ↘ Spec (.of k)) (𝟙 Z) z), Function.Injective α ∧ Function.Exact α β ∧ Function.Surjective β ∧ (∀ (U : X.Opens) (hz : i z ∈ U) (a : Γ(X, U)) (ha : (i.stalkMap z) (X.presheaf.germ U (i z) hz a) = 0), α (conormalStalkFibreClass i z ⟨X.presheaf.germ U (i z) hz a, ha⟩) = relativeDifferentialsStalkFibreGerm (X ↘ Spec (.of k)) i z U hz a) ∧ (∀ (U : X.Opens) (hz : i z ∈ U) (a : Γ(X, U)), β (relativeDifferentialsStalkFibreGerm (X ↘ Spec (.of k)) i z U hz a) = relativeDifferentialsStalkFibreGerm (Z ↘ Spec (.of k)) (𝟙 Z) z (i ⁻¹ᵁ U) hz (i.app U a))
lean.note: The canonical arrows are specified by their values on generating differential germs. Helpers package existing tensor products, the stalk functor, ideal cotangent classes, and the existing universal derivation. Since the stalk map is surjective and its kernel annihilates its cotangent quotient, tensoring this quotient over R is canonically tensoring over S = R/I. The landed stalk-functor node is added to stmt_deps.
